title: Common length of maximal prime chains
statement: For a field k and a finite type k-algebra domain S, there is d : ℕ with ringKrullDim S = (d : WithBot ℕ∞), and every maximal prime LTSeries in S has length d.

proof.text: Choose n and a surjective polynomial presentation f using Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''. Mathlib Ideal.primeSpectrumOrderIsoZeroLocusOfSurj identifies Spec S with the primes containing ker f, by comap. Map any strict chain into the polynomial spectrum. Its length is at most the height of its last prime (Order.length_le_height_last), hence at most n by the polynomial height bound. Thus ringKrullDim S is finite; it is not bottom since S is a domain.

In any finite-dimensional partial order a longest LTSeries is maximal. Otherwise its head is not minimal, its last is not maximal, or a consecutive pair is not a cover: cons, snoc, or insertNth increases its length. A saturated finite chain with minimal head and maximal last is a maximal chain: for a point comparable with every term, choose the first term above it; minimality or the preceding cover forces equality. These are the proved private helpers longest_isMaxChain and saturated_isMaxChain.

A maximal prime chain b starts at the zero prime, ends at a maximal ideal, and has only cover steps. Indeed inserting any point below the head, above the last, or between consecutive terms would give a larger chain; comparability with each term gives the needed insertion. Transport b by comap. Its head is ker f and its last is maximal (Ideal.comap_isMaximal_of_surjective). A prime strictly between two transported terms contains ker f, so the inverse prime correspondence would contradict their cover relation. The polynomial height-difference theorem applies. The height of the last ideal is n by MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_localizationAtMaximal and IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height. Therefore b.length = n - height(ker f) in ENat.

Apply the same length formula to any maximal chain and to the longest chain, which is maximal by the second step. Injectivity of the natural-number cast gives equality of their lengths. Order.krullDim_eq_length_of_finiteDimensionalOrder identifies the length of the longest chain with ringKrullDim S. Take this length as the required natural number d.

lean.statement: theorem finiteTypeDomain_ringKrullDim_localizationAtMaximal_chains {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] [IsDomain S] : ∃ (d : ℕ), ringKrullDim S = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∀ (p : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum S)), IsMaxChain (fun q r : PrimeSpectrum S ↦ q ≤ r) (Set.range p) → p.length = d
